import json

# Each option is checked against the plan's two goals:
#   G1: relieve understaffed security (requires competent, available workers)
#   G2: ease economic hardship of impoverished students (requires the aid to reach them)
# An option "questions the plan" if it shows the plan fails or misdirects a goal.
options = {
    "A": {"text": "Non-going-home students are not all financially struggling",
          "undermines_G2": True,   # aid goes to non-needy students too
          "undermines_G1": False},
    "B": {"text": "Students are hardly competent for the security task",
          "undermines_G1": True,   # workers can't fill the security gap
          "undermines_G2": False},
    "C": {"text": "Limited funds versus a large number of non-going-home students",
          "undermines_G1": True,   # plan cannot be carried out as intended
          "undermines_G2": True},
    "D": {"text": "Most non-going-home students signed up for winter English tuition",
          "undermines_G1": False,  # says nothing about security capacity
          "undermines_G2": False}, # says nothing about whether aid reaches the needy
}

questioning = {k: (v["undermines_G1"] or v["undermines_G2"]) for k, v in options.items()}
non_questioning = [k for k, q in questioning.items() if not q]

assert len(non_questioning) == 1, "expected exactly one option that cannot question the plan"
final_answer = non_questioning[0]

print(json.dumps({
    "final_answer": final_answer,
    "evidence": {
        "questions_plan": {k: questioning[k] for k in options},
        "goals": ["G1 relieve security understaffing", "G2 ease economic hardship"],
        "non_questioning_count": len(non_questioning),
    },
}))
